discovery: Foundational theory of active matter: flocking and the hydrodynamics of self-propelled ordered phases

nominees.name: Sriram Ramaswamy
nominees.affiliation: Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore, India

subfield: Soft condensed matter and statistical physics (active matter)
motivation: Landau theory, broken symmetry and Goldstone modes underpin our understanding of materials. These nominees showed that the framework must be rebuilt when the constituents themselves consume energy and move. Vicsek's 1995 minimal model revealed a nonequilibrium ordering transition in self-propelled particles. Toner (with Tu) built its hydrodynamic theory and proved that flocks show true long-range orientational order in two dimensions, which the Mermin-Wagner theorem forbids at equilibrium. Ramaswamy (with Simha) showed that active nematics are generically unstable and predicted giant number fluctuations, both later confirmed in bacterial suspensions, cytoskeletal extracts and vibrated granular layers. Their work created a new state of matter governed by symmetry and conservation laws rather than detailed balance. It reorganized soft-matter and biological physics and gave a field its standard tools, including the active defect dynamics now studied worldwide.
